# Delegate narrative - United Arab Emirates (generated by HISN for the ITU AI Readiness Simulation Game)

Domain: governance of AI systems in telecom networks that decide whether essential health and government messages reach citizens (AI SMS filtering, network AI failover).

D10 AI & Policies: binding instruments exist for health-data localisation (Federal Law No. 2 of 2019, Art. 13) and operator spam duties (TDRA Unsolicited Electronic Communications Policy v1.1), but filtering duties cover marketing spam rather than fraud, and no instrument assigns authority over operators' AI filter changes.

D13 Digital Infrastructure: sender identity is not authenticated end-to-end; a policy sandbox shows sender authentication plus a verified-sender lane would raise protection and access together.

Identified gaps:
- G1: Telecom filtering duties cover marketing spam, not fraud or impersonation (instrument_verified)
- G2: Government senders lack protected / authenticated-sender status (instrument_verified)
- G3: AI content-scanning of health SMS for fraud lacks an explicit legal basis (instrument_verified)
- G4: No emergency fast-path for AI-triggered failover of health data (instrument_verified)
- G5: No instrument assigns authority to approve, override or require protection in operators' AI filters (system_discovered)

Measured results (synthetic sandbox): see docs/headline_numbers.md in the HISN repository.
